questions.prompt: Where should a command-timeout check run so that it still works when commands stop arriving?
options: Only when a new sensor message arrives.
Inside the command callback, before applying the command.
On an independent timer that compares now with the last command stamp.
questions.explanation: A check inside the data callback never runs when data stops.

questions.prompt: v=1.0 m/s, deceleration 2 m/s^2, total reaction time 0.1 s. Stopping distance in m, precision 0.001.
Clearance 1.5 m, deceleration 2 m/s^2, reaction time 0.1 s. Maximum speed in m/s, precision 0.001.
Hazard with severity 3 (of 4) and likelihood 4 (of 5). Risk score S x L.
A range sensor returns NaN. What should the safety layer do?
options: Average it with the next valid sample so the control loop sees no gap.
Treat it as a fault and go to the safe response; never clip or ignore it.
Replace it with the previous valid value silently and keep the controller running.
Clip it to the maximum range and continue, since that is the safest reading.
questions.explanation: Invalid data must not become plausible data.

questions.prompt: After a timeout fault, valid commands start arriving again. What should happen?
options: Resume at once using the new command, because the fault condition has ended.
Stay stopped until an explicit reset, then require fresh valid data.
Restart the whole computer so every process begins from a clean state.
Resume at the last speed before the fault, since it was known to be safe.

questions.prompt: Write a four-row hazard table for a small mobile robot (cause, harm, S, L, class, mitigation) and mark which mitigations remove, protect or warn.
rubric: Each row has a concrete cause and harm with severity and likelihood.
Mitigations are ordered remove > protect > warn, including at least one software limit and one non-software measure.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
